description:
Declare numeric stats on threads, log values against them, and show those values over time.

Subcommands:
  new NAME --thread THREAD --type TYPE --agg AGG — declare a stat in the thread file's frontmatter
  list [--json] — list declared stats
  log NAME VALUE [-d DATE] [-t HH:MM] — add a value to buffer.md; `buffer flush` files it in the thread's daily log
  series NAME [--by PERIOD] [--since D] [--until D] [--json] — value per day, week or month, from logs plus the unflushed buffer

Args:
  NAME   lowercase letters, digits and '-'; unique across the vault; put a unit in the name where unclear (run-km, spend-zar)
  VALUE  whole number for an int stat; plain number for a decimal stat (12.50, never 1e3)

Flags:
  new:
    --thread THREAD   required; 'Kind/Name', name or wikilink
    --type T          required; int|decimal (int for counts, steps, events)
    --agg A           required; sum|last|max; how a period's values combine: sum adds, last takes latest, max takes largest
  list:
    --json
  log:
    -d, --date YYYY-MM-DD  default today
    -t, --time HH:MM       default now
  series:
    --by day|week|month    default day; weeks start Monday
    --since / --until YYYY-MM-DD
    --json                 periods with no values show '-' (null in JSON), not 0

Examples:
  ["new", "pushups", "--thread", "Topics/Fitness", "--type", "int", "--agg", "sum"]
  ["log", "pushups", "25"]
  ["log", "run-km", "5.2", "-d", "2026-10-07"]
  ["series", "pushups", "--by", "week", "--json"]

Notes:
  To record an event (yes/no), declare an int stat and log 1 each time it happens. With sum, the series counts occurrences. With max, it shows whether the event happened at all.
  There is no rename or delete. To change a declaration, edit the thread frontmatter. Values already logged are not rewritten.
  Exit 1: nothing is written and the reason goes to stderr. Causes: name not declared or declared twice, value of the wrong type, bad -d/-t format, a bad or taken name on `new`, a thread that does not resolve, or --since after --until.
  Exit 2: usage error (missing argument, or unknown --type/--agg).
